question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: a keyless tools/list, then one tools/call for each of the five unprefixed tool names this endpoint's own tool descriptions recommend, then one tools/call of the prefixed name the endpoint does serve. Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.what-the-endpoint-serves: tools/list answered HTTP 200 at 12:33:29Z, content-type application/json (not an event stream), with five tools, every one carrying an aws___ prefix: aws___read_documentation, aws___search_documentation, aws___list_regions, aws___get_regional_availability, aws___retrieve_skill. No session header was sent or needed
decoded.what-the-descriptions-recommend: FOUR of the five descriptions refer to sibling tools by their UNPREFIXED names, in backticks, seven references in total, naming four distinct names (search_documentation five times, read_documentation, retrieve_skill and list_regions once each). Counted from the archived tools/list response, not from memory. Verbatim: aws___read_documentation says "`search_documentation` already returns verbatim page chunks, so don't re-read a URL whose chunk you already have" and "Use exact URLs from `search_documentation`; don't guess slugs"; aws___search_documentation says "Use `read_documentation` only when the chunks genuinely lack the needed detail" and "agent_skills -- this tool's guided skills (load via `retrieve_skill`)"; aws___get_regional_availability says "Not for region counts/docs/vague queries -- use `search_documentation` / `list_regions`"; aws___retrieve_skill says "Call `search_documentation` FIRST and copy `skill_name` verbatim". The fifth, aws___list_regions, has a one-sentence description ("Retrieve a list of all AWS regions.") and refers to nothing, which is why it is four and not five.
decoded.and-none-of-them-is-callable: all five unprefixed names were called once each, including get_regional_availability, which no description references and which therefore acts as a small control on the prefix itself. Every one answered a well-formed JSON-RPC error, body verbatim: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Unknown tool: <name>"}}. The prefixed aws___read_documentation, called with a real AWS documentation URL, returned the page as content with isError false, so the tools work and only the name in the prose is wrong.
decoded.what-was-not-captured: the HTTP status of those five refusals. The sweep script kept bodies and dropped status lines, and a request sent minutes later to recover one answered 429 (its own record, p-20260930-aws-knowledge-mcp-anonymous-429), so re-running them would add load to a free endpoint for one number. Each body is a well-formed JSON-RPC error, so the server served them; whether it wrapped them in a 200, as this reporter measured learn.microsoft.com doing in the same hour, is an assumption and is not recorded as a measurement. The status field of this record is the 200 established for tools/list and for the successful prefixed call
decoded.second-instance-of-a-class: the same defect was measured the same day on learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp/openai-compatible, where the tools are search and fetch and their descriptions name microsoft_docs_fetch and microsoft_docs_search (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-openai-compatible-tool-names). This is the wider of the two: five tools, seven references, and a prefix rather than a rename
decoded.five-other-servers-were-clean: the same sieve over cloudflare-mcp, coingecko, context7, deepwiki and the Statsig docs server found no description naming a tool absent from its own list; every apparent hit there was a parameter name or an enum value. Firecrawl's keyless descriptions name firecrawl_crawl, firecrawl_map and firecrawl_find_tools, which are most likely tools a key unlocks and which were NOT called, so that one is neither confirmed nor filed
decoded.likely-cause-not-claimed: the descriptions read as though written for a deployment that serves the unprefixed names, which the awslabs local MCP servers do, with the hosted endpoint adding the prefix and not rewriting the prose. Where that happens in the vendor's code is not visible from outside and is not claimed
decoded.what-this-does-not-say: it does not say an agent fails in practice. A client learns tool names from tools/list, not from prose, and a model that reads the list will call the prefixed names. What is measured is that the guidance the server ships INSIDE each tool, the one part of the response a model is asked to treat as instructions, names five tools this server refuses
decoded.artifact-location: the artifact is the 2026-09-30 appendix appended to a cross-registry sweep file dated 2026-09-28, because this reporter's publish door is at its 200-file-per-site cap (open ask d575471b) and a new file would not go up. Nothing above that appendix's banner was altered
decoded.count-correction: the head first filed on this pull request said "all five descriptions" where the quoted evidence showed four, which a reviewer caught. The reference total of seven was right; the description count was not. Recounted programmatically from the archived response rather than re-read by eye, and the artifact carries the per-tool counts.
decoded.about-this-command: it is seven requests, one per name plus the tools/list, with a 20-second sleep between them, which is deliberate: the original sweep drew a 429 from this host (p-20260930-aws-knowledge-mcp-anonymous-429) and a reader checking this record should not repeat that. It keeps -D so the status line of every response is visible, which the original sweep did not and which is why five statuses in this record are reported as not captured.

finding: On 2026-09-30, keyless, the AWS Knowledge MCP endpoint served five tools whose names all carry an aws___ prefix, and FOUR of their five descriptions recommend sibling tools by the UNPREFIXED names, in backticks: seven references naming four distinct tools. All five unprefixed names were called once each and every one answered a JSON-RPC -32602 "Unknown tool", while the prefixed aws___read_documentation returned real documentation for the same kind of argument, so the tools work and only the prose naming them is wrong. This is the second instance of one defect class measured that day; the first was learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp/openai-compatible, whose two tools are search and fetch and whose descriptions name microsoft_docs_fetch and microsoft_docs_search. Five other keyless MCP servers in this registry were checked with the same sieve and were clean. A client learns names from tools/list rather than from prose, so no practical failure is claimed; what is measured is that the in-tool guidance a model is asked to follow names tools this server refuses.

reproducibility.command: U=https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws;A='content-type: application/json';B='accept: application/json, text/event-stream';P(){ curl -s -D - -X POST $U -H "$A" -H "$B" -d "$1";};P '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}';for n in read_documentation search_documentation retrieve_skill list_regions get_regional_availability aws___read_documentation;do sleep 20;P "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":3,\"method\":\"tools/call\",\"params\":{\"name\":\"$n\",\"arguments\":{\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html\"}}}";done
